newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, then gains after AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, then gains after AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, helped by a spate of short covering on colder weekend weather forecasts, ended higher Wednesday in moderate trade, then moved up further after a bullish weekly AGA stock report.
March closed 5.2 cents higher at $2.016 per million British thermal units, then climbed to $2.03 on ACCESS after the report. April settled 2.5 cents higher at $2.004.

"It's (the AGA number) more than people thought, but overall, it's a non-event. People aren't going to need gas in March," said one Texas-based trader, noting a sizeable stock surplus to last year, particularly in the eastern region.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 147 bcf, well-above average expectations in the 110-125 bcf range. But traders noted overall inventories were still 143 bcf, or 14.5 percent over year-ago. And eastern stocks, which fell last week by 97 bcf, were still 233 bcf, or 51 percent, above last year, a factor likely to weigh on prices in late winter and early spring.
Chart traders still pegged support in March at Tuesday's low of $1.85 and then at the contract low of $1.749. Resistance was seen at $2.08-2.09 and then $2.25-2.30.

On the physical side, prices Wednesday were propped up by colder weekend weather forecasts. Gulf Coast prices gained about 10 cents to the $1.90 area. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to the mid-$1.70s. New York city gate gas was steady to up slightly at about $2.20.
The 12-month strip rose 3.3 cents to $2.094. NYMEX said an estimated 46,295 Hub contracts traded, down slightly from Tuesday's revised tally of 47,273.
NYMEX March Hub natgas expires Monday, Feb 24.
NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas did not trade Wednesday.

On the KCBT, March finished 0.4 cent higher at $1.71, while most deferreds ended up by one cent. The East/West spread widened by 4.8 cents to 30.6 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 149 lots changed hands, down from Tuesday's total of 272.
Physical prices in the Permian basin gained more than five cents Wednesday to the mid-to-high $1.60s.
